what: joint demographic pool for ssb.synth.draw_profiles: the six target moderators + weight (7,196 cells)

sources.persons: /workspace/datasets/acs/downloads/unix_pus/psam_pus{a,b}.sas7bdat (ACS 2018 1-year PUMS), AGEP>=18, non-group-quarters; 2,414,823 person records, PWGTP-weighted to 246.0M adults (3.1% of weighted adults dropped as GQ)
sources.housing: /workspace/datasets/acs/downloads/unix_hus/psam_hus{a,b}.sas7bdat joined on SERIALNO for HINCP (household income). HINCP is non-missing for 100% of non-GQ adults - OPEN.md item 1 is closed by the mount.
sources.panel_composition: /workspace/datasets/voelkel2026 (design twin: census-quota US opt-in panel, n=13,821)

recodes.gender: SEX 1=Male 2=Female; 'Other' injected exogenously (ACS has no such category)
recodes.race: HISP != '01' -> Hispanic / Latino (precedence), else RAC1P 1/2/6 -> White / Black / Asian, else Other
recodes.income: household HINCP x ADJINC(1.013097), cut at the target's nominal edges 30k/56k/100k/168k
recodes.party: not in ACS. P(party | age_band x gender x race x education x income) estimated on CES 2024 (weighted) with a hierarchical fallback (drop income -> drop gender -> drop age -> race only -> pooled) whenever a conditioning cell carries < 30 weighted units; the ACS cell weight is then split across the four party levels by that conditional.

gender_Other.source: voelkel2026 (0.93%), which asks the target's exact 3-level gender item; CES gender4 gives 0.76% (recorded, not used)
gender_Other.allocation: by age band using the CES age profile of gender-Other respondents (18-29: 3.0%, 60+: 0.2%), gender-neutral within the other five moderators

income_instrument.why: ACS supplies the JOINT (true dollars, correlated with education/race/age); the target measures SELF-REPORTED household income in an online panel, which is the CES instrument. ACS 2018 dollars applied to the target's nominal 2026 edges land closer to the CES 2024 self-report than any inflation-adjusted variant (L1 distance 0.198 at f=1.00 vs 0.323 at f=1.15, 0.409 at f=1.25), so no inflation factor is applied and the margin is raked onto CES. See OPEN.md item 1.

education_panel.why: the target study quotas on age, gender and race/ethnicity only, so education falls where an opt-in panel puts it. The design twin (same panel type, same year) is 37.3% BA-or-more vs the census 30.9%, and 29.2% HS-or-less vs the census 38.9%. The three-way collapsed margin is raked onto the twin; the split WITHIN each collapsed group (e.g. Master's vs Doctorate) stays ACS.

party_instrument.why: CES pid3 (Rep/Dem/Ind/Other) is the target's own 4-option self-ID item. The twin panel's ANES branching item folds leaners into Dem/Rep and gives 34.1/33.0/31.2/1.8 - recorded as a diagnostic, not used, because the instruments differ.

raking.method: IPF, 7 passes to max margin deviation 2.6e-07
margins: age_band x gender x race (census quota, ACS)

caveats: ACS is 2018 and the target fields in 2026: the pool is a joint distribution raked to 2026-relevant margins, never a birth-year shift.
Hispanic precedence is a rule, not a fact (see notes/DATA_format.md 1.3).
party is imputed, so party x (education, income) associations are CES's, and any party x race interaction finer than the fallback cell is smoothed.

pool_of_record.variant: party-association raked (2-way party x {income, education, race, age_band, gender} margins from CES conditionals, on top of the census 3-way, education-3 and income margins)
pool_of_record.why: MEASURED, run 20260815-dryrun-02. The hierarchical party imputation flattens party's association with the other moderators: against a CES-native pool the party x race table was off by up to 3.95 pp of the sample, party x income by 1.21 pp. Two-way raking cuts that to 0.94 and 0.30 pp. The cost is <=0.79 pp on the census race marginal and 0.93 pp on the party marginal (itself only a CES estimate). It matters to a SCORED row: with the flattened pool the synthetic Demographic predictability R^2 is 0.302 (policy_general) and 0.328 (concern_mean); with the realistic associations it is 0.268 and 0.286. Uncorrelated moderators explain MORE variance additively, so the flattened pool EXAGGERATES demographic predictability - which is exactly what that scoring row punishes. G6/G7 are unchanged (tier2mod RMSE 2.462 -> 2.476, sd ratio 0.989-1.009).
pool_of_record.sensitivity_variant: inputs/pool/joint_marginal_exact.csv - the same pool with census marginals exact and party associations flattened. Use it to re-run any analysis that depends on the quota being exact.
